feat: decompose inverse images of branch discs (#22173)

This PR constructs disjoint power coordinates over the entire inverse image of a sufficiently small target disc and its closure. Each disc upstairs is centered at a point of the central fibre, has exponent equal to its analytic local multiplicity, and has radius satisfying `rₓ ^ mₓ = δ`. Compactness excludes additional sheets outside the chosen charts. Closed source discs stay inside the coordinate domains, so they are compact embedded discs, and both open- and closed-disc preimage equalities are exposed.

Advance [FuchsianOrbifolds/README.md, Layer 5, item 3](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/blob/main/FuchsianOrbifolds/README.md#layer-5-compact-surface-degree-theory-and-fuchsian-applications), the branched-cover Euler-characteristic formula and `RiemannSurface.riemannHurwitz`, serving completion milestone 6. Its prescribed excision proof needs whole inverse images of small branch discs to be disjoint unions of power-coordinate discs. Main already has individual holomorphic normal forms, finite ramification, and the covering away from branch values; this supplies their missing disc-decomposition input without assuming the desired global decomposition. After this PR, the milestone still needs the compact-surface Euler characteristic and genus, finite-cover Euler-characteristic multiplicativity on the disc complement, and the gluing count deriving Riemann–Hurwitz.

The cofinite Dirichlet-polygon path has overlapping open work, while this analytic input is distinct from the open polygon, elliptic thin-part, and triangle-presentation PRs. Scan all open PR descriptions, recent merged PRs, pinned Mathlib, and Tau Ceti before implementation and again during self-review. The cooperative claim returned the documented exit-2 permission fallback. No unmerged work is imported.

Add `TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/RiemannSurface/Branch/Discs.lean` (176 lines), exporting only `TauCeti.RiemannSurface.exists_disjoint_power_charts`. Allow arbitrary prescribed source neighbourhoods and any target chart in the maximal holomorphic atlas. Neither source nor target connectedness, target compactness, surjectivity, nor a nonempty central fibre is required; nonconstancy is the existing pointwise neighbourhood condition. Reuse `exists_chart_eq_pow_localMultiplicity`, `finite_preimage_singleton`, finite Hausdorff separation, and Mathlib's real-power and norm-power lemmas. Credit the existing fibre-multiset separation argument in the module, together with Forster §§4 and 17 and Miranda II §4. No Mathlib infrastructure or external formalization is vendored.

Apply the required common-prefix directory organization, relocating the existing branch-values module unchanged and updating its sole importer, `RiemannSurface/Polynomial.lean`. No declarations are renamed and no forwarding module is retained.

| Old module | New module |
| --- | --- |
| `TauCeti.Analysis.Complex.RiemannSurface.BranchValues` | `TauCeti.Analysis.Complex.RiemannSurface.Branch.Values` |

Read the shared protocol and all ten rubrics: scope, correctness, reuse, attribution, api-design, generality, placement, naming, documentation, and proof-quality. Self-review retains a single existential construction, indexes charts only by the actual fibre, names the repeated multiplicity-positivity fact, and makes the required module move. Repeated source searches find no replacement for the whole-disc decomposition. Importing examples check the ramified fibre of the sphere squaring map, the source-radius equation and compactness of its closed source disc, and the empty-fibre case.

Local validation passes: `lake exe cache get`, whole-library `lake build --iofail` (53,376 jobs), the importing examples, and the changed-module axiom check (3 modules, 44 compiled declarations, zero violations). The scope recipe reports `full: deleted module: TauCeti/Analysis/Complex/RiemannSurface/BranchValues.lean` because of the module move. This requires full CI; the local axiom check reads only the changed existing modules, not their transitive imports. Changed-module environment lint also passes with zero violations. These are local checks; CI verifies the pushed head.
